title: Build peer review sub-agent
description: Create an agent in agents/ that acts as a bar raiser for PR/FAQ drafts. System prompt is adversarial: 'your job is to find weaknesses, not confirm strengths.' Given a .tex draft, it reads critically and returns structured flags: unsupported claims, ambiguous language, judgment calls missing FAQ cross-references, risk ratings that don't match evidence, citation gaps. Does NOT have write access — only generates questions. The main agent evaluates each flag: accept (revise), reject (explain why), or escalate (surface to user). Loop until no critical issues remain.

title: Add ux-bar-raiser.md reference guide
description: Add a reference guide for the UX Bar Raiser lens to skills/prfaq/references/ux-bar-raiser.md. Owns the Usability risk dimension. Should cover the full customer journey, cognitive load of onboarding, mental model alignment, accessibility, error recovery, and the 'would I switch from my current workflow' gut check. Should also sharpen the Customer Quote and Getting Started sections, not just the usability risk rating. Invoked during Phase 3 external FAQs and Phase 2 getting started.

title: Add principal-engineer.md reference guide
description: Add a reference guide for the Principal Engineer lens to skills/prfaq/references/principal-engineer.md. Owns the Feasibility risk dimension. Should cover architecture trade-offs, operational complexity at scale, build vs. buy decisions, dependency risk, data model choices that are hard to reverse, and the 'hardest unsolved technical problem' question. Invoked during Phase 3 technical FAQs.

title: Add biblatex citation system to template
description: Add biblatex support to the LaTeX template and compile pipeline. The template should use \usepackage[style=authoryear]{biblatex} with a generated .bib file. The compile script needs a biber pass between pdflatex runs. All factual claims in the PR/FAQ should use \cite{key} for real sources (web, research papers, market reports, primary research from ./research/). The skill workflow should instruct the main agent to generate .bib entries as citations are added. The research agent populates these entries.

title: Add judgment-to-FAQ cross-referencing
description: When the PR/FAQ makes a judgment call (e.g. 'Product X prioritizes A over B to eliminate frustration with C'), it should cross-reference a specific FAQ that explains the reasoning via LaTeX \label/\ref. Each faqpair environment gets an optional \label{faq:slug}. Judgment calls in the press release use 'see FAQ~\ref{faq:slug}' to link to the reasoning. The corresponding FAQ should unpack the judgment: why do we believe this, what evidence supports it, what's the risk if we're wrong. The peer review agent verifies that every judgment call has a corresponding FAQ.

title: Build research sub-agent
description: Create an agent in agents/ that serves as a research librarian for the main prfaq skill. Interface: given a claim or topic, search for evidence and return structured citations (source, URL/path, summary, relevance). Tools: WebSearch, WebFetch, Glob, Read (for ./research/). Returns biblatex-formatted citation entries. Architecture should anticipate MCP server expansion — the agent's prompt stays stable while data source connectors grow (Statista, Google Scholar, SEC/EDGAR, Census/BLS, CRM, product analytics). Each connector would be an MCP server in .mcp.json.

title: Add unit-economics.md reference guide
description: Add a reference guide for unit economics to skills/prfaq/references/unit-economics.md. Owns the Viability risk dimension. Should cover CAC, LTV, LTV:CAC ratio, payback period, gross margin, contribution margin. Help distinguish products where unit economics matter (SaaS, marketplace) from ones where they don't (open source, internal tools).

title: Support quarry-mcp as optional research data source
description:
Add optional integration with quarry-mcp (https://github.com/jmf-pobox/quarry-mcp) as a data source for the research sub-agent. Quarry provides semantic search over the user's entire local file corpus — PDFs, images, notes, source code, scanned documents — via MCP.

This replaces the need to cherry-pick files into ./research/. Instead, the research agent can query 'customer interviews about onboarding friction' or 'market sizing for developer tools' and get relevant chunks from anywhere the user has indexed.

Implementation:
- Add quarry as an optional MCP server in the plugin's .mcp.json (or document how users add it)
- The research agent checks if quarry tools (search_documents, get_page) are available. If yes, use them as a primary search source alongside WebSearch and ./research/ files.
- If quarry is not installed, fall back gracefully to current behavior (./research/ scan + web search)
- The research agent should use quarry's collection filtering if the user has organized documents into collections (e.g., a 'research' or 'interviews' collection)
- Citations from quarry results should include the source file path and page/chunk reference

This is the first third-party data source connector for the research agent, establishing the pattern for future integrations (Statista, EDGAR, Google Scholar, etc.).
